battle.name: 第一次宋遼戰爭
battle.brief: 太平興國四年十一月，宋太宗以收復燕雲為名自太原東征，連拔淤口、雄州、涿州，直抵南京幽州。遼援軍三萬精騎夜襲岐溝宋營，宋軍大潰，太宗乘驢車夜遁涿州，北伐功敗垂成。卡面希臘重步兵並未出現於此役，其重盾互蔽、以矛陣抵禦騎兵的原理，正是宋軍以神臂弓、霹靂炮與長槊結陣所循的路線。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 第一次宋遼戰爭自太平興國四年（979）十一月宋太宗親征起，至太平興國七年（982）閏九月遼軍最後一次深入宋境止，是北宋立國後對遼第一次大規模野戰。宋一方以皇帝趙光義為最高統帥，中軍由禁軍宿將曹彬率領並隨侍帝側，另以潘美鎮太原、策應西路，諸道州兵自河北、山東、關中抽調，分為東、中、西三路北上；前線指揮權集中於帝與數名宿將，糧秣調度則由三司與諸路轉運使承擔。禁軍是此役唯一具備長途作戰與夜戰經驗的骨幹，州兵多只負責守城、徵發與護糧。遼一方以攝政的蕭綽為實際決策者，幼帝耶律隆緒居中坐殿，南面樞密使韓德讓總攝漢地軍政，北面大將耶律休哥、耶律斜軫等率契丹、奚部重騎北上，東京、西京與南京留守分供人馬器械。遼的南北面官制使它同時擁有草原騎兵與漢地州縣的步兵、攻城器械，這種混編結構是它在本土防守戰中仍能反守為攻的關鍵；此役中原與河北正面留下的記載多為宋方修史所敘，遼軍番漢混編的實際比例與各路兵團番次，只能從《遼史》與宋方零星奏議中推得大概。
countriesEn: The First Song-Liao War began with the personal northern expedition of Emperor Taizong in the eleventh month of the Taiping Xingguo era (979) and lasted until the ninth intercalary month of the Taiping Xingguo era (982), when the Liao made its last deep incursion into Song territory. It was the first large-scale pitched battle fought by the Northern Song against the Khitan since the dynasty's founding. On the Song side the supreme commander was the emperor, Zhao Guangyi, himself; the central column was led by the veteran imperial-guard commander Cao Bin, who remained at the emperor's side, while Pan Mei held Taiyuan and covered the western approach, and troops levied from the circuits of Hedong, Hebei, Shandong and Guanzhong marched north in three columns, east, centre and west. Operational command was concentrated in the emperor and a handful of seasoned generals, while the movement of grain and materiel fell to the finance commissioners and the circuit transport officers. The imperial guards were the only troops in the Song army with genuine experience of long marches and night operations; the provincial levies were used mainly for garrison duty, requisition and escorting supply. On the Liao side the real decision-maker was the regent, the Dowager Consort Chengtian, Xiao Chuo, with the child emperor Yelü Longxu enthroned in the middle; the Southern Commissioner of Military Affairs, Han Derang, took charge of administration and warfare in the Chinese-held territories, while generals such as Yelü Xiuge and Yelü Xiazhen led the Khitan and Xi heavy cavalry north from the Eastern, Western and Southern capitals, the residents of each providing men and equipment. The Liao's dual northern and southern command structure gave it grassland cavalry and Han Chinese infantry and siege equipment at the same time, and that mixed force was what allowed it to turn defence into offence on its own ground. Most of what survives about the fighting on the central plain and in Hebei comes from Song historiography; the true proportions of Khitan and Han troops inside the Liao armies, and the tribal composition of each column, can only be approximated from the History of Liao and from scattered Song memorials.
people: 宋太宗趙光義是此役的推手，也是受創最深的人。他即位後銳意取燕雲，太平興國四年春滅北漢，即打算乘勝東進；朝中有老臣上書反對，說北漢新降、太原人心未定，遼國必乘虛來攻，若師出無名而輕進，恐一敗而不可收拾。太宗不聽，反以急於乘勝為由，於十一月親率大軍東下。岐溝兵敗後，他乘驢車夜馳涿州，沿途諸軍散失，殘兵由曹彬收集而後與帝會合；這一役對其身心是沉重打擊，正史記載他此後手足痹痛、行走不便，多有學者認為與岐溝的驚悸及舊疾有關，卻無從確證。曹彬是禁軍宿將，全程在太宗左右，兵潰之際收拾散卒，護駕至涿州；潘美坐鎮太原，負責西路與糧道；潘美部將楊業於本役末段在雁門一線以少量騎兵邀擊遼軍，斬獲數百級，是宋軍在這一輪戰事中少數明確的勝利記錄，楊業其後在雍熙北伐的陳家谷口兵敗被擒，後事慘烈。遼方真正決定戰局的是承天蕭綽。宋軍逼近南京時，她致書宋太宗，以南北和好二十餘年、今若大舉南征恐為後世所笑相勸，未被採納，遂親率大軍赴援。耶律休哥承擔正面反擊，耶律斜軫領精銳夜襲宋太宗本營，兩人自此名重於宋。韓德讓以漢人樞密使身分居中調和，主張持重，與主戰的契丹諸將意見相左。雙方書信往還、使者往返頻繁，韓德讓與蕭綽一系的和談取向，實際上為其後二十餘年的邊境對峙定了基調。
peopleEn: Song Taizong, Zhao Guangyi, was the man who set this war in motion and the one who suffered most from it. Since his accession he had been determined to recover the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun, and in the spring of the fourth year of the Taiping Xingguo era, when he destroyed Northern Han, he meant to carry the campaign further east. Court elders petitioned against this, arguing that the newly taken Northern Han was still unsettled in its loyalty, that Taiyuan's people were not yet attached, that the Liao would certainly strike while the Song army was absent and exposed, and that an advance made without just cause, and made lightly, could bring about one defeat from which there would be no recovery. The emperor refused, treating haste as the very ground for advance, and in the eleventh month he led the army east in person. After the rout at Qigou he fled by donkey cart to Zhuozhou through the night, his columns scattering along the way, the remnants gathered up by Cao Bin before they rejoined the emperor; the campaign left a deep mark on his body and mind. The official record describes a paralysis of his hands and feet and difficulty of movement from this point on, and many scholars connect it to the shock of Qigou and to an old condition, though no proof exists. Cao Bin, a veteran of the imperial guards, stayed with the emperor throughout, collected the broken troops after the collapse and brought the ruler safely to Zhuozhou. Pan Mei sat at Taiyuan, responsible for the western approach and the supply line. Pan Mei's subordinate Yang Ye, in the closing phase of this war, ambushed Liao cavalry with a small force in the Yanmen area and took several hundred heads, one of the few clear Song successes of the entire round. Yang Ye would later be captured after the defeat at Chenjiagu in the Yongxi northern expedition, and his end was grim. The figure who truly decided the Liao side was the Dowager Consort Chengtian, Xiao Chuo. When the Song army closed on the Southern Capital she sent a letter to Emperor Taizong, pointing out that the two states had been at peace for more than twenty years and that a great southern campaign now would bring shame upon the pages of later historians. The argument was ignored, and she marched in person with a great army. Yelü Xiuge took the frontal counter-stroke, Yelü Xiazhen led picked cavalry in the night attack on the emperor's own camp, and from this campaign both men became celebrated in Song accounts. Han Derang, a Chinese scholar-official serving as Commissioner, sat in the middle arguing for caution and was out of step with the Khitan generals who favoured the offensive. Letters and envoys passed continually between the two courts, and the negotiating line held by Han Derang and the dowager's party in practice set the tone for more than twenty years of standoff along the frontier.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是希臘重步兵，配備於公元前五世紀的希臘城邦，裝束為圓盾、短劍與兩米長的刺槍，年份標為公元前五百年，遠早於這場戰爭。979年的河北戰場上沒有任何一支希臘式方陣，這一點必須先說清楚：宋軍的步兵用刀、長槊、手版與弩，遼軍的主體是騎兵，兩者的技術譜系與希臘城邦毫無關聯。但這張卡仍有可說的位置，因為它指向的是重裝步兵對重裝騎兵這一古老的對位問題。希臘重步兵的戰力不來自個人，而來自盾牌相接形成的正面厚度，矛尖在方陣邊緣構成拒馬，軍心由左右鄰卒的物理存在決定。同一原理在宋軍身上換了形狀：北宋邊軍結陣時以長槊如林、拒馬鹿角遮蔽騎兵，弓弩手居陣後或側後，床子弩與神臂弓在陣前射擊，故有宋人言宋軍之長在以弩制騎。裝備細節上，宋軍用札甲、葛布甲、藤甲與皮甲，攻城備有雲梯、撞竿、望樓、霹靂炮與火箭；遼軍則以奚人、契丹的皮毛裝備與馬鎧為主，攻城用撞車、飛石與火箭，番漢兵混編時更換裝具甚速。雙方共同的瓶頸是馬匹與糧秣：宋軍北伐靠步軍與運糧車，車隊在太行陘道與河北平原上拉得極長；遼軍的坐騎由諸部供給，乾酪與粟麥隨軍同行，因此能在戰區內機動作戰而不必依賴長線後勤。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Greek hoplite, equipped in the Greek city-states of the fifth century BC, with a round shield, a short sword and a two-metre thrusting spear, and it is dated to 500 BC, long before this war. There was no Greek-style phalanx anywhere on the Hebei battlefield in 979, and that must be stated plainly at the start: Song infantry carried sabres, long spears, small hand shields and crossbows, while the Liao fielded cavalry as its main strength, and neither technical lineage has anything to do with the Greek city-states. The card still has a place to occupy, because it points to the old alignment of heavy infantry against heavy cavalry. The fighting power of a Greek hoplite did not come from the individual but from the thickness a joined line of shields produced, with the spear points along the edge of the phalanx acting as a bristling hedge, and with morale held in place by the physical presence of the neighbour on either side. The same principle took a different shape in the Song army: when the Northern Song border troops formed up they screened the cavalry with a forest of long spears and rows of anti-cavalry stakes, crossbowmen stood behind or on the flanks, and traction crossbows and heavy sinew bows shot from the front of the line, which is why Song writers said the strength of the Song army lay in using the crossbow to check the horse. On equipment, the Song used lamellar armour, hemp cloth armour, rattan armour and leather, and for assault they carried scaling ladders, battering poles, watch towers, thunder-crash bombs and fire arrows. The Liao relied on the hide gear of the Xi and Khitan with their own horse armour, and for assault used battering cars, flung stones and fire arrows, swapping equipment with great speed as Khitan and Han units were mixed. The shared bottleneck for both sides was horses and supply: the Song expedition moved on infantry and baggage wagons, and the wagon train stretched out enormously along the Taihang passes and the plains of Hebei; the Liao drew their mounts from the various tribes and carried dried milk and millet with the army, which allowed them to manoeuvre inside the theatre without depending on a long rearward line.
tactics: 宋軍的戰術體系，是一套典型的進攻方略被直接搬到平原會戰上。太宗自太原出發，東取井陘關道，經常山、定州，進抵莫州淤口，再攻雄州、涿州，企圖沿河北平原的交通線直取南京幽州。渡黃河一段因冰薄未成，改由東路攻拔淤口，反映出計畫中對河防的顧慮。作戰序列上，前線以弩砲齊射與砲石打擊遼軍密集隊形為先手，步兵結陣後進，騎兵在兩翼與後方策應；但此役最關鍵的還是糧道。糧車由太原經井陘、正定一線輸送，越過太行山道之後隊列拉長、速度下降，護糧兵力必須從戰鬥序列中抽調，這在後人解釋岐溝之敗時被反覆提及。遼軍的戰術完全相反：主力不急於攻堅城，而是以三萬精騎集結於涿州西南的岐溝一帶，先以小股騎兵挑釁、牽制宋軍前鋒，待宋太宗主力自鼓山方向壓上，再以兩翼重騎同時衝擊宋軍的薄弱處，徹夜糾纏，把宋軍的指揮系統與士氣一併拖垮。遼軍攻城極少正面硬撞，寧可先用飛石與火箭覆蓋城頭，逼宋軍閉門不出，再尋間隙別攻；定州、涿州兩城因此都未被攻下。追擊階段，耶律休哥以精騎緊追宋太宗潰軍至涿州城下，逼宋軍丟棄重裝與輜重而退。三年之中，遼軍還在山西方向作戰，攻代州、蔚州一帶，因宋軍有備、糧秣難以接續而未能深入，多半巡騎掠地而歸。
tacticsEn: The Song tactical system was a textbook offensive plan set down unchanged on a plain battlefield. The emperor left Taiyuan, took the Jingxing pass road east, passed through Changshan and Dingzhou, reached Mozhou and Yukou, then struck at Xiongzhou and Zhuozhou, intending to run straight down the traffic lines of the Hebei plain to the Southern Capital at Youzhou. The planned crossing of the Yellow River failed because the ice was too thin, and the army turned east instead to take Yukou, which shows how carefully the plan had allowed for the river defences. In the order of battle, the front was opened with volleys of crossbows and with stones and bombs thrown into the dense Liao formations; infantry followed in formed ranks, with cavalry in the wings and in the rear. But the decisive factor in this campaign was still the supply line. The grain wagons ran from Taiyuan through Jingxing and Zhengding, and once they were over the Taihang track the column lengthened and slowed, and the escorts for the food had to be taken out of the fighting order, a point repeated every time later writers explained the defeat at Qigou. The Liao tactical concept was the exact opposite: the main force was in no hurry to attack a walled city, but concentrated thirty thousand picked horsemen around Qigou southwest of Zhuozhou, first sending small bodies of riders out to provoke and hold up the Song vanguard, and then, once the emperor's main body came down off Gus Mountain, striking the weak points of the Song line with heavy cavalry on both wings at once, tangling with it through the whole night and dragging down the Song command system and morale together. When the Liao did attack a city it rarely hit the wall head-on; it preferred to cover the parapet first with flung stones and fire arrows, forcing the Song to keep the gates shut and then look for a side door, which is why Dingzhou and Zhuozhou both held. In the pursuit, Yelü Xiuge drove the broken Song troops hard against the walls of Zhuozhou, forcing the Song to abandon heavy equipment and baggage to get away. Across the three years the Liao also operated in Shanxi, striking at Dai Prefecture and Wei Prefecture, but with the Song alert and their own supply hard to sustain they did not push deep and mostly returned after riding raids.
data: 與史實有關的數字可分兩類：一是時間，二是兵力。太宗於太平興國四年（979）十一月自太原發兵，十一月內連下淤口、雄州、涿州，岐溝之敗亦在同月，其後十二月至次年正月在河北收拾殘局、鞏固邊防，遼軍南下反攻延續到太平興國七年（982）閏九月，整場戰爭前後約三年。里程方面，太原經井陘、定州至雄州、涿州，全程接近八百里，其中太行陘道一段是全軍補給的瓶頸。兵力上，《宋史》記此次調禁軍及諸道州兵合計二十餘萬，但名籍數與實際攜行量差距極大，真正投入岐溝正面的，是以禁軍為主的數萬精銳。遼軍方面，岐溝一戰投入的精騎通常記為三萬，《遼史》與部分宋人奏議另見十萬之說，後者當是含各路番漢兵團的總數，而非一處集中的兵力。距離上，岐溝距涿州城數十里，鼓山在營地西側，太宗自鼓山下山夜遁，行程數十里即抵城下。戰果方面，遼軍一度攻取君子泊、固安、下曲陽等河北城鎮，太宗乘驢車退涿州時攜帶極少；而楊業在雁門一線以數百騎邀擊遼軍，斬首數百級、擒獲遼將數人，是此役宋軍唯一有明確斬獲數字的記錄。以上數字多有互相牴觸之處，引用時宜取其概數，不宜當作精確統計。
dataEn: The figures that can be tied to the record fall into two kinds: time and strength. The emperor set out from Taiyuan in the eleventh month of the fourth year of the Taiping Xingguo era (979); within that month Yuku, Xiongzhou and Zhuozhou fell, and the defeat at Qigou came in the same month. From the twelfth month into the first month of the following year the campaign was spent restoring order in Hebei and reinforcing the frontier, and the Liao counter-offensives ran on into the ninth intercalary month of the seventh year of Taiping Xingguo (982), so the war as a whole lasted about three years. As for distance, the road from Taiyuan through Jingxing and Dingzhou to Xiongzhou and Zhuozhou came to close on eight hundred li, and the stretch of the Taihang pass was the bottleneck for the whole army's supply. On strength, the History of Song records that the imperial guards together with the provincial levies of the various circuits mustered to over two hundred thousand, but the gap between the muster roll and what actually marched was enormous; what was committed to the front at Qigou was the several tens of thousands of picked men drawn chiefly from the guards. On the Liao side, the cavalry committed at Qigou is usually given as thirty thousand, while the History of Liao and several Song memorials give a figure of a hundred thousand, which must be read as the total of all columns of Khitan and Han troops rather than a single concentrated force. For distance again, Qigou lies some tens of li from the walls of Zhuozhou, with Gus Mountain west of the camp, and the emperor's flight down the mountain and through the night covered only a few tens of li before he reached the city. On results, the Liao took such Hebei strongholds as Junzi Po, Gu'an and Xiaquyang for a time, and the emperor carried almost nothing with him when he retreated to Zhuozhou by donkey cart; while Yang Ye, with several hundred riders, ambushed Liao cavalry in the Yanmen area and took several hundred heads and a number of Liao officers, the one engagement in this war for which the Song side has a clear record of kills. These figures contradict one another in several places, and it is better to treat them as rough magnitudes than as precise statistics.
cause: 打起來的理由分宋遼兩層。宋太宗滅北漢後，得到的不是安寧而是新的隱患：北漢是遼一手扶植的前朝餘孽，新城新附，人心未定，而太原正卡在宋遼之間最要衝的位置上。朝廷中有老臣據北漢降將的風聞上書，說劉崇當年曾屢次入寇、疲宋師於奔命，如今宋方先取太原，遼必以此為可乘之機，請太宗慎動。太宗不聽，反而認為北漢既平、士氣正盛、糧草亦足，此時不取燕雲，待遼國完成部署便再無機會，於是給自己找到了收復燕雲十六州的名分與理由——這是第一次宋遼戰爭最深的一層動機：北宋不滿於被動防守，企圖用一次成功的北伐把邊境推到燕山南麓，同時藉此把新附的河北與太原納入同一套軍政秩序。遼方的理由則是被迫應戰。蕭綽在宋軍越過太行、逼近南京之後才主戰，理由不是好戰，而是幽州一旦失守，契丹與漢地就再無縱深；她先試圖以書信勸止，見無效後才傾力出擊。制度層面上，宋朝剛建立三十年，禁軍人數龐大但北伐經驗不足，馬匹與遠征補給能力有限；遼則坐擁草原兵源與漢地糧秣，能在本土作戰中不斷以輕騎襲擾、待其疲竭再行決戰。雙方的能力邊界與戰略抱負，在岐溝這一次交鋒中正面碰撞。
causeEn: There are two layers of reason, one on each side. After destroying Northern Han, Song Taizong did not gain peace but a fresh anxiety: Northern Han had been a client state propped up by the Liao, the new city was newly taken and its loyalties unsettled, and Taiyuan sat squarely on the most critical ground between the two states. Court elders took up a report from a surrendered Northern Han officer and petitioned the throne, saying that Liu Chong had repeatedly invaded and worn down the Song army with endless marches, and that now that the Song had taken Taiyuan first, the Liao would certainly take this as its chance; they urged the emperor to be cautious. He refused, arguing that with Northern Han destroyed the morale was high and the grain was sufficient, and that if Yan and Yun were not taken now, once the Liao completed its dispositions the chance would never return. That is how he found for himself the title and the justification of recovering the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan and Yun. This is the deepest motive behind the First Song-Liao War: the Northern Song was not content with passive defence, and wanted one successful northern expedition to push the frontier up to the southern foot of the Yanshan, and at the same time to fold the newly taken Hebei and Taiyuan into a single military-administrative order. The Liao's case was that it was forced to fight. Xiao Chuo only turned to war after the Song had crossed the Taihang and closed on the Southern Capital, and her reason was not bellicosity but the fact that once Youzhou fell there would be no depth left for either the Khitan or the Chinese lands; she first tried to stop the campaign by letter, and only when that failed did she commit everything. At the level of institutions, the Song had stood for barely thirty years: its imperial guards were numerous but short on experience of northern expeditions, and its horses and its ability to supply a long march were limited. The Liao, with grassland sources of troops and Chinese sources of grain, could keep harassing with light horse in home territory and then strike once the enemy was exhausted. The two sides' limits of capability and their strategic ambitions came into direct collision at Qigou.
impact: 這場戰爭沒有改變邊界，卻改變了兩個政權對彼此的認識。宋朝方面，失敗的直接後果是先取燕雲的戰略宣告破產，北伐從攻勢轉為守勢。此後十餘年，河北沿線的塘泊、邊城、屯兵與弩砲配置成為國策重點，軍費重心由中央禁軍向河北四路轉移，專門對付遼國鐵騎的技術——神臂弓、床子弩、霹靂炮、拒馬與陷馬坑——在邊軍中加速普及，而《武經七書》體系的整理也在此一背景下展開。對宋太宗本人，岐溝之敗是一道難以平復的傷痕：此後他的手足之疾與體能衰退被多處記載，他本人亦以封禪泰山、大修禮樂來重建統治的正當性，反而招來史家對其以封禪掩敗的議論。國際層面上，第一次宋遼戰爭開啟了宋遼之間漫長的試探期，雙方都用這次交手互相摸底：宋軍知道正面野戰與遠征補給非其所長，遼庭知道深入河北平原容易因糧秣斷絕而陷入泥潭，於是有了二十餘年的邊境相持，最終走到1004年的澶州之役與1005年的澶淵之盟，用歲幣換取邊界，雙方和平延續百餘年。西北方向則出現了另一層後果：宋朝把主要兵力東調對遼，留給西北的空間被壓縮，黨項首領李繼遷乘機擴張，攻取夏州、銀州等地，迫使宋廷在981至982年間改以招撫與市易羈縻，承認其夏州刺史的名號，西夏由此坐大，日後成為替宋更難纏的第二大邊患。就兵器觀而言，此役還提供了一個千年反覆的樣本：當一方沒有希臘重步兵那樣相互遮蔽的重裝步兵時，靠弩砲與長槊結陣同樣能短暫抵住騎兵衝鋒，但代價是重兵、耗彈與對地形的苛刻要求。
impactEn: This war changed no frontier, but it changed how the two governments understood one another. For the Song, the immediate consequence of the defeat was the collapse of the strategy of taking Yan and Yun first; the northern campaign turned from an offensive into a defensive posture. For more than a decade afterwards the ponds, frontier cities, garrisons and crossbow batteries along the Hebei line became a priority of state policy, military spending shifted from the central imperial guards towards the four Hebei circuits, and the techniques built specifically against Liao heavy cavalry — the heavy sinew bow, the traction crossbow, the thunder-crash bomb, anti-cavalry stakes and horse-pits — spread quickly through the border armies, while the compilation of the Seven Military Classics took place against this background. For Song Taizong himself the defeat at Qigou left a wound that never closed: his paralysis of the hands and feet and his decline are recorded in several places, and he answered it with the grand sacrifice on Mount Tai and an elaborate programme of ritual and music to re-establish the legitimacy of his rule, only to draw the judgement of historians that the grand sacrifice was a screen for the defeat. At the international level the First Song-Liao War opened a long period of testing between the two states, and each side used the encounter to measure the other: the Song learned that open-field battle and expedition supply were not its strengths, and the Liao court learned that pushing deep onto the Hebei plain invited entanglement through a severed supply line. What followed was more than twenty years of standoff along the frontier, ending in the campaign at Chanzhou in 1004 and the Chanyuan Treaty of 1005, in which the payment of silk and silver bought the border and peace that held for more than a century. A second consequence ran in the opposite direction: with the main effort of the Song drawn east against the Liao, the space available in the northwest was compressed, and the Tangut leader Li Jiqian expanded, taking the prefectures of Xia and Yin, forcing the Song court between 981 and 982 to fall back on pacification and trade arrangements and to recognise his title as military governor of Xia Prefecture. Western Xia grew out of that, and became in time the second and far more intractable frontier problem for the Song. In the study of arms this campaign also furnished a recurring model across the centuries: where one side had no interlocking heavy infantry of the Greek hoplite kind, a screen of crossbows and long spears could hold off a cavalry charge for a time, at the price of heavy infantry, heavy expenditure of bolts and severely demanding ground.
result: 岐溝之戰的結果對宋軍是慘敗。遼軍夜襲之後，宋太宗本營被突破，禁軍主力潰散，趙光義在鼓山下失去控制，連夜乘驢車奔涿州，途中數度迷路，殘兵與器械大量遺棄。遼軍乘勝攻取君子泊、固安、下曲陽等地，前鋒直抵涿州、定州城下，兩城守軍依城固守，遼軍一時不能下，遂在河北平原上展開掠地式的戰役。定州、涿州未破，幽州南京自然無恙，宋太宗一舉取燕雲的計畫徹底破滅。遼軍此後數年再攻山西，攻至代州、蔚州一線，因宋軍有備、糧秣難以接續，也未能深入，多半以巡騎掠地而還。整場戰爭下來，邊界大致回到原狀：宋守住山西與河北的主要城鎮，遼保住了南京與燕雲山前的縱深，雙方都沒有取得決定性成果，卻都付出了代價——宋軍損折精銳，太宗威望受損，遼軍雖勝而遠征消耗亦重，被拖進了它原本打算避免的長期消耗戰。真正解決問題的不是這場戰爭，而是其後二十五年所累積的均勢：1004年宋真宗御駕澶州，遼軍南下直逼黃河，雙方在兵臨城下之際達成協議，1005年簽訂澶淵之盟，宋朝每年輸遼歲幣銀絹，換取宋遼為兄弟之國、燕雲歸於遼的長期和平。從第一次宋遼戰爭到澶淵之盟，二十五年的邊疆經驗終於換來一句明白的結論：宋無法用一場戰爭取回燕雲，只能用可以負擔的代價買回時間。楊業在雁門的勝利是這一輪宋軍唯一提振士氣的記錄，而他在其後北伐中的悲慘結局，也預示了北宋此後對遼的每一次北伐，都將重複同一條教訓。
resultEn: The result at Qigou was a disaster for the Song. After the night attack the emperor's own camp was broken into, the main body of the imperial guards scattered, Zhao Guangyi lost control below Gus Mountain and fled by donkey cart towards Zhuozhou through the night, losing his way more than once and abandoning a great part of his troops and equipment. The Liao followed up by taking such places as Junzi Po, Gu'an and Xiaquyang, their vanguard reaching the walls of Zhuozhou and Dingzhou, where the garrisons held fast behind the walls and could not be taken at once, so the campaign settled into a sweep of the Hebei plain. Since Dingzhou and Zhuozhou held, Youzhou, the Southern Capital, was of course safe, and the emperor's plan to take Yan and Yun in one stroke was dead. For several years afterwards the Liao attacked again in Shanxi, reaching the line of Dai and Wei, but with the Song on its guard and their own supply hard to sustain they too could not push deep, and mostly rode back after raids. Across the whole war the border came back roughly where it had started: the Song held the main cities of Shanxi and Hebei, the Liao kept the Southern Capital and the depth in front of the Yanshan, and neither side gained a decisive result, yet both paid for it. The Song lost picked troops, the emperor lost standing, and the Liao won but spent heavily on an expedition it had hoped to avoid, drawing itself into the long war of attrition it had tried to escape. What actually settled the question was not this campaign but the balance of strength accumulated over the following twenty-five years: in 1004 Emperor Zhenzong of Song marched in person to Chanzhou when the Liao drove down to the Yellow River, and the two sides came to terms with armies at the river; the Chanyuan Treaty of 1005 followed, the Song paying the Liao silk and silver every year in return for the two states being acknowledged as brothers and Yan and Yun remaining with the Liao, a long peace that held. From the First Song-Liao War to the Chanyuan Treaty, twenty-five years of frontier experience finally produced one plain conclusion: the Song could not take Yan and Yun back in a single war, it could only buy back time at a price it could afford. Yang Ye's victory at Yanmen was the one record in this round that lifted Song morale, and the grim end that overtook him in the later northern expedition foretold that every Song campaign against the Liao from that point on would repeat the same lesson.
